card: This pull request updates Tapscript Miniscript duplicate-key checks to compare public keys as 32-byte x-only keys rather than 33-byte compressed keys. Previously, tr() descriptors containing keys that differed only in parity byte passed sanity checks even though both branches serialize to identical scripts on-chain. This violated BIP-379 duplicate key requirements and allowed third parties to malleate transactions by altering branch selectors with a single signature. P2WSH descriptors continue to distinguish 33-byte compressed keys.
changed_since_previous: Updated KeyConverter::KeyCompare in src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp alongside descriptor.cpp to apply x-only comparison under Tapscript context in the Miniscript test harness.
evidence: Commit 53439006c6 and PR description: 'Because a single signature satisfies both branches, third parties could malleate transactions by altering branch selectors without holding private keys, violating BIP-379 non-malleability invariants.'
Fixes linked issue #36414 ('descriptor: tr() duplicate-key check misses keys that differ only in parity').
problem: When a tr() Miniscript descriptor contains keys that differ only in parity prefix (such as pk(02X) and pk(03X)), duplicate-key sanity checks pass because the keys are compared as 33-byte CPubKeys. However, Tapscript serializes keys on-chain without parity, causing both branches to produce identical scripts; this violates BIP-379 duplicate key restrictions and allows third parties to malleate transactions by switching execution branches without possessing private keys.

risk.why: A flaw in descriptor validation could improperly reject valid Tapscript descriptors or fail to prevent malleability issues in spending scripts.

summary: Compares public keys as 32-byte x-only public keys instead of 33-byte compressed keys during Miniscript duplicate-key checks in Tapscript descriptors. In a Tapscript context, keys sharing an x-coordinate but differing only in parity byte are now detected as identical, causing DuplicateKeyCheck() to fail and reject the descriptor as not sane. Segwit v0 (P2WSH) descriptors continue to distinguish 33-byte compressed keys.
